edition.name: Migne PL 3 (1844), Epistola Firmiliani ad Cyprianum, via Corpus Corporum / Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Qualis vero error sit et quanta sit caecitas ejus qui remissionem peccatorum dicit apud synagogas haereticorum dari posse, nec permanet in fundamento unius Ecclesiae, quae semel a Christo supra petram solidata est, hinc intelligi potest quod soli Petro Christus dixerit: Quaecumque ligaveris super terram, erunt ligata et in coelis; et quaecumque solveris super terram, erunt soluta et in coelis; et iterum in Evangelio quando in solos Apostolos insufflavit Christus dicens: Accipite Spiritum sanctum. Si cujus remiseritis peccata, remittentur illi; et si cujus tenueritis, tenebuntur. Potestas ergo peccatorum remittendorum Apostolis data est et Ecclesiis quas illi a Christo missi constituerunt, et episcopis qui eis ordinatione vicaria successerunt. Hostes autem unius catholicae Ecclesiae, in qua nos sumus, et adversarii nostri, qui Apostolis successimus, sacerdotia sibi illicita contra nos vindicantes et altaria profana ponentes, quid aliud sunt quam Chore et Dathan et Abiron, pari scelere sacrilegi, et easdem quas et illi poenas daturi cum his qui sibi consentiunt, secundum quod etiam tunc illorum participes et fautores pari cum eis morte perierunt.
pass_a_gloss: What kind of error it is and how great blindness is of him who says that remission of sins can be given in synagogues of heretics, and does not remain in foundation of one Church, which once was solidified by Christ on rock, from this it can be understood that Christ said to Peter alone: Whatever you bind on earth, will be bound also in heavens; and whatever you loose on earth, will be loosed also in heavens; and again in Gospel when Christ breathed on only Apostles saying: Receive Holy Spirit. If you remit sins of anyone, they will be remitted to them; and if you retain of anyone, they will be retained. Therefore power of remitting sins was given to Apostles and to Churches which they, sent by Christ, established, and to bishops who succeeded them by vicarious ordination. But enemies of one Catholic Church, in which we are, and adversaries of ours, who have succeeded Apostles, vindicating to themselves illicit priesthoods against us and setting up profane altars, what else are they than Core and Dathan and Abiron, with equal crime of sacrilege, and they will give same punishments as those, with those who consent to them, according to which also then participants and favorers of them perished with same death as they
pass_b_english: You can see the kind of error and the depth of blindness in anyone who claims that remission of sins can be granted in the synagogues of heretics, yet refuses to remain in the foundation of the one Church that Christ once established on the rock. It becomes clear from this that Christ spoke to Peter alone: "Whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven" (Matt. 16:19). And again in the Gospel, when Christ breathed on the Apostles only, he said: "Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive anyone's sins, they are forgiven; if you retain anyone's sins, they are retained" (John 20:22–23). Therefore the power to remit sins was given to the Apostles, to the Churches they established when sent by Christ, and to the bishops who succeeded them by vicarious ordination. But the enemies of the one Catholic Church—the Church in which we stand—and our adversaries, who claim to have succeeded the Apostles, are seizing illicit priesthoods for themselves against us and erecting profane altars. What are they but Korah, Dathan, and Abiram, guilty of the same sacrilegious crime? They will suffer the same punishments as those rebels, along with those who side with them, just as the participants and supporters of that ancient rebellion perished by the same death.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass B correctly identifies and adds the required inline scripture citations (Matt. 16:19 and John 20:22–23) which were alluded to in the Latin and glossed in Pass A. The names Chore, Dathan, and Abiron are rendered as Korah, Dathan, and Abiram in Pass B, which is an acceptable English transliteration of the biblical figures. All clauses, including the comparison to the rebellion of Korah, are preserved.

source: 'Quaecumque ligaveris super terram, erunt ligata et in coelis; et quaecumque solveris super terram, erunt soluta et in coelis;', english: 'Whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven' (Matthew 16:19)
